fin_note: With vs. without philanthropy: stripped of grants, September's consolidated operating result (EBITDA) was a loss of $439,510 — right on forecast (−$440,652) and about $145K better than a year ago (−$584,362). YTD, the EBITDA loss of $1.77M beats forecast by $749K and has narrowed ~45% YoY (from −$3.21M). Philanthropy was light in September ($17K vs. $133K forecast, grant timing), so adjusted net income was −$422,487 for the month and +$714,883 YTD. Revenue of $1.40M came in $116K under forecast, almost entirely print circulation (−$123K); advertising beat forecast by $11K. Expenses of $1.84M ran $118K under forecast (advertising −$77K, distribution −$40K, finance/admin −$28K), partly offset by IT ($26K over, on staffing and Newzware migration costs). *Adjusted net income excludes future pledges, grant-covered start-up costs, interest income, and depreciation.
fin_revmix_note: The one growing line: digital circulation revenue is up 16.1% YTD (and +5.3% in September) — every print line and digital advertising are down double digits YoY. Digital subscriptions remain the only organic revenue engine that is growing.
audience_note: Steep pullback vs. a much stronger comparable week: sessions, users, and engaged sessions were all down roughly a quarter to a third YoY this week (sessions −24.7%, users −30.8%, engaged sessions −25.9%) against last October's higher baseline. Pages/session improved to 1.62 (+20.1% YoY) as repeat-visit share held up much better than new-visitor traffic (new visitors −28.7% vs. repeat visits −16.6%), pushing the repeat-visit share to 51.0% from 46.0% a year ago. YTD the softness is more moderate but still broad-based: sessions −14.7%, engagement rate down 5.1 pts, and session duration down 16.9% YoY, while repeat-visit share YTD still edges out last year (49.7% vs 49.1%).
channels_note: Watch: Email/newsletter drives ~3% of sessions (the top-of-funnel capture gap); "Unassigned" is ~17% of weekly traffic and ~16–17% YTD, a UTM/tagging-hygiene gap that weakens attribution.

subs_note: Print/digital split refreshed to the August by-term Subscription Report. Of 46,738 active subs, 68.9% (32,216) are print and 31.1% (14,522) digital (~14,116 paid). Encouraging shift: new subscriptions rebounded to 691 in August (from 504 in July) and net adds climbed to +122 (from +27) — the acquisition slump that had halved new subs YoY is easing. Print stays extremely sticky (~0.25%/mo churn); the dedicated Sports Pass holds 693. Year-over-year and YTD subscription trends aren't in the single-month by-term export — those will populate from the Piano API.
